title: Replace fixed-millisecond delay polling with emitsInOrder stream matchers in points_balance_dao_test.dart watchBalance tests
why: The two watchBalance tests collect stream emissions into a list via `.listen(emissions.add)` then assert on `emissions.last` after fixed 20ms/50ms sleeps. Under CI contention (parallel shards, a throttled runner) the reactive Drift query stream may not have emitted the post-write value before the sleep expires, producing an intermittent failure on `expect(emissions.last, 50)` that has nothing to do with a real regression — the classic flaky-test pattern that gets 'fixed' by rerunning rather than investigated. profile_dao_test.dart in this same batch (watchProfilesByAccount test) shows the deterministic alternative already in use elsewhere: `expect(stream, emitsInOrder([...]))`, which waits for the actual emission instead of racing a clock.
recommendation: Rewrite both watchBalance tests to assert via `expect(db.pointsBalanceDao.watchBalance(1), emitsInOrder([0, 50, ...]))` (or expectLater) registered before the mutating calls, matching the pattern already used by profile_dao_test.dart's watchProfilesByAccount test, instead of manually collecting emissions behind a fixed sleep.
acceptance_criteria: Both watchBalance tests in points_balance_dao_test.dart use emitsInOrder/expectLater with no fixed-millisecond Future.delayed used purely to wait for a stream emission
Tests pass repeatedly under both default and constrained (--concurrency=1, or CI-like throttled) runs
Rule-0 checker: grep test/**/*_test.dart for `Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds` occurring in the same test body as a preceding `.listen(` call
